purpose: Taranis is a suite of Slicer scripted modules for voxel-based Y-90 radioembolization dosimetry, lung shunt fraction, CBCT territory planning, and AI-assisted liver/lung segmentation. It is aimed at researchers and clinical physicists working with SPECT/PET/CT in Slicer.
summary: No malicious or concealed behaviour found in the files read. Model downloads are SHA256-checked and user-confirmed, and MONAI is installed with --no-deps after confirmation. Main concerns: the CBCT module installs scikit-image with its dependencies into Slicer's shared Python without --no-deps, and model weights are loaded with torch.load. Licence is MIT. Coverage is partial: I read about a quarter of the ~20k lines and did not read Taranis.py, dosimetry.py or the other large modules in full.

safety.rationale: Model downloads go to a fixed GitHub release URL with SHA256 checks and a user prompt (Taranis/TaranisLib/ai.py:165-177, LSFcalc/LSFcalc.py:1301-1316). Weights are loaded with torch.load without weights_only (ai.py:437), so a tampered local .pth in a user-chosen folder could run code. No telemetry or outbound data upload was found in the searches.

environment.rationale: CBCTPlanning/CBCTPlanning.py:822 runs a plain pip_install of scikit-image, which can pull or upgrade shared packages such as numpy or scipy. The MONAI path correctly uses --no-deps (Taranis/Taranis.py:2166). The module-level sys.path.append fallbacks in three module files are generic.

packaging.rationale: CMakeLists files list the Python and resource files I checked. EXTENSION_DEPENDS is "NA" and build_dependencies is empty, while the runtime needs the PyTorch extension (optional) and TotalSegmentator (optional); this is documented in-app. banner.png (about 1.7 MB) is duplicated in four module folders, and the repository holds several multi-MB JPEG/PNG screenshots.

license.rationale: LICENSE is MIT (Copyright 2025 Burak Demir), which permits distribution. Model weights come from SlicerAether, whose licence I did not check. TotalSegmentator liver-lesion tasks are non-commercial only, and the README and UI state this.

soundness.rationale: Inference runs on the main thread with a WaitCursor and no progress (ai.py:440-444). Temporary files are cleaned up in finally blocks (dicomexport.py:163-209, dosimetry.py:1520-1531). Several test CMake entries for the submodules are commented out.

utility.rationale: README.md is long (~530 lines) with a user manual, a sample-data pointer, and clear research-use disclaimers shown in the UI (Taranis.py:104-105). Unit tests exist under Taranis/Testing/Python. Clinical use is explicitly disclaimed.

findings.title: CBCT planning installs scikit-image with dependencies into Slicer's shared Python
findings.explanation: The user is asked to confirm, but the install is a plain pip_install with no --no-deps, so scikit-image's declared requirements (numpy/scipy/etc.) can be upgraded or changed in Slicer's shared environment and affect other extensions. The MONAI path already avoids this with --no-deps. Requirements are not pinned, so a downgrade of a bundled package is possible through transitive dependencies.
findings.suggestion: Install with --no-deps after checking that numpy/scipy/imageio/etc. are already present, or pin a compatible version range and document the change in the confirmation dialog.

findings.title: torch.load of model weights without weights_only
findings.explanation: Weights are loaded with torch.load(modelPath) from any file found in user-selected or module folders. The download path verifies SHA256, but files already on disk, or files placed in the custom AI models folder, are trusted without a checksum. On PyTorch versions where weights_only defaults to False, a malicious .pth can execute code on load. Exposure is limited to users who place untrusted files in those folders.
findings.suggestion: Pass weights_only=True to torch.load (state_dict only), and verify the SHA256 of local files when they match a known model name.

findings.title: Same torch.load pattern in the LSF calculator
findings.explanation: LSFcalc loads the same weights the same way, so the same risk applies to the LSF module's model folders.
findings.suggestion: Use weights_only=True and share the verified loader between the two modules.

findings.title: sys.path.append with a generic path at import time in three modules
findings.explanation: When TaranisLib cannot be imported, these modules append a Taranis folder to sys.path. This is a global side effect at import in Slicer's process and may pick up an unrelated TaranisLib package. It is only reached in the fallback branch.
findings.suggestion: Rely on the extension's CMake install, which already installs TaranisLib next to each module, or remove the fallback for release builds.

findings.title: Large binary images committed to the repository
findings.explanation: banner.png (about 1.7 MB) is duplicated in four module Resources folders, and several multi-megabyte screenshots and JPEGs are in the repository root. These bloat the clone and are not needed at runtime beyond the icon and banner.
findings.suggestion: Keep one shared copy of the banner and move the large screenshots to a release asset or external URL, which EXTENSION_SCREENSHOTURLS already references.

findings.title: Licence of downloaded model weights not stated in what was reviewed
findings.evidence: Taranis is released under the **MIT License**.
findings.explanation: The app downloads model weights from the SlicerAether release, but the licence of those weights is not stated in this repository. The extension's MIT licence covers only the code. TotalSegmentator-based liver-lesion tasks are non-commercial only, and the README and UI state this.
findings.suggestion: State the licence of the downloaded model weights (SlicerAether release) and the TotalSegmentator terms in the README.

findings.title: Tests for submodules are not registered with CTest
findings.explanation: The per-module Testing/Python CMakeLists for LSFcalc, easy_reg, and the dosimetry modules only contain commented-out slicer_add_python_unittest calls. Only the hub has unit tests wired into the build, so regressions in those modules would not be caught by CI.
findings.suggestion: Register the existing module tests, or remove the empty test directories.

not_checked: Taranis/Taranis.py, Taranis/TaranisLib/dosimetry.py, cbct.py, vascular.py, controller.py, segtools.py, workflow.py, and most other large modules were not read in full; findings there are unverified.
LSFcalc/LSFcalc.py, RadioembolizationDosimetry* and easy_reg.py were only sampled through search hits.
The scm_revision is 'main' (a moving branch); the reviewed source snapshot is not pinned to a commit.
No CI results or test runs were available; the test suite was not executed.
Licence terms of the SlicerAether model weights and the SampleImages data were not checked.
Large binary files (screenshots, banner) were listed but not inspected.
questions_for_author: Why is scikit-image installed without --no-deps, and have you checked that its dependencies do not change numpy or scipy in Slicer?
Can torch.load be called with weights_only=True for both the Taranis and LSF model loaders?
What is the licence of the SlicerAether model weights, and are they cleared for redistribution through your download?
Can you pin scm_revision to a tagged commit instead of 'main'?
